findings.title: website_name bypasses trust-level restrictions and leaks private website info
findings.body: The new `:website_name` attribute is added to the main `attributes` list but is not included in `untrusted_attributes` (unlike `:website`). As a result, when a TL0 user's profile is viewed by an anonymous user and `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` returns true, the `website` attribute is hidden, but `website_name` is still serialized because its inclusion logic only checks `website.present?`. This leaks the user's website host and path to anonymous visitors, violating the privacy controls applied to other profile fields. The `include_website_name` method also lacks a trailing `?`, potentially causing it to be ignored entirely, which would make the attribute always present even when `website` is empty. The spec at line 11 of `spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb` omits `:website_name` from `untrusted_attributes`, so this regression is not caught.

findings.title: Domain comparison treats sibling subdomains as the same domain
findings.body: The condition in the `elsif` branch compares the suffix after the first label: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]`. This means any two domains with more than two labels that share the same parent after the first label are considered equivalent. For example, `www.example.com` and `forum.example.com` would both match, causing the full URL path to be shown for any website hosted on a sibling subdomain of the instance domain, even though they are not the same domain nor a parent/child relationship. The PR description and tests only cover exact domain match and parent-child relationships (e.g., `example.com` vs `forums.example.com`), so this behavior is likely unintentional and may expose a misleading display of the website path. Additionally, the conditional uses a ternary inside an `elsif` containing a comparison that returns a boolean, possibly making the intent unclear.
